summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed=false). The gate failed because the custom experiment has no blocks and no power_w object (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false), so the final verdict is blocked and comparison_valid=false. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so even if it had run it would produce only a steady-state result with no transient trace. The paper's observable is a transient time-until-hotspot (TUH) of 0.2 ms (5th percentile, 7nm, idle warmup; 25th/50th percentiles 0.4/0.6 ms, and 14nm 0.4/0.6/1.2 ms). It comes from a 3D-ICE v3.0.0 transient co-simulation with Sniper and McPAT, a layered vertical stack with heatsink and fan, and hotspot criteria of T>80 C and MLTD>25 C within 1 mm. No Studio output exists, so no numerical comparison is made. Any 2D steady temperature would differ in location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions, so only qualitative sensitivity could be discussed, such as smaller 7nm cores and higher power density shortening TUH. This is not an exact replication and no replication is claimed. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes and powers were provided. No illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated, so there is no source commit or placement assumption to report. The linked HotGauge GitHub repository and Zenodo archives (DOIs 5523504 and 5523535) were not pinned or inspected, and their contents are unverified. Only Table I areas (5, 2.5 and 1.25 mm2 per core), the 3:2 core aspect ratio, the 5 GHz/1.4 V operating point and the bzip2 power density lower bound (>8 W/mm2) are available. These cannot be turned into per-block coordinates or watts without an unpublished rule.
limitations: Studio was skipped; there is no simulation output, so no temperature, TUH or MLTD comparison is possible.

The gate failed: the custom experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w object. The floorplan block coordinates and per-block powers are not published numerically (Fig. 5 is image-only and no Sniper/McPAT power values are given).

Essential physical mismatches: the paper's TUH is a transient hotspot-detection time (3D-ICE, idle/cold warmup, 1M-cycle steps), whereas the experiment is a steady-state custom 2D run with no transient trace.

Mismatches in boundary assumptions: the paper uses a layered vertical stack (active and bulk silicon, solder TIM, copper spreader, thermal grease, HS483-ND heatsink with P14752-ND fan at 6000 rpm) and a 40 C local ambient; no Studio package or material assumptions are provided to match this.

Mismatches in aggregation and location: the paper reports a 5th-percentile TUH across SPEC2006 benchmarks and cores, anywhere on the die, using hotspot criteria (T>80 C and MLTD>25 C within 1 mm) that are not temperature-only observables.
The paper's time-varying per-unit workload power traces cannot be reproduced by any single-row power input.

Linked assets (GitHub, Zenodo 5523504, Zenodo 5523535, PDF) were not pinned or inspected. Adversarial checks and the independent page/asset review are unresolved, and one evidence item lacks a valid locator.
The die area is ambiguous: the paper states about 5 mm2 for the die, while Table I gives 5 mm2 per core at 14nm. The core orientation for the 3:2 aspect ratio is unspecified.
Nothing here establishes exact replication of the paper's results. The gate-controlled final verdict is not_2d_applicable with comparison_valid=false.

The paper observable is a transient time-until-hotspot (TUH, a hotspot-detection time) from a time-resolved 3D-ICE simulation. A steady-state or single-row-power-trace 2D run cannot reproduce it.

The thermal stack is a layered vertical model: active layer plus bulk silicon, solder TIM, copper heat spreader, thermal grease and a HS483-ND heatsink with a P14752-ND fan at 6000 rpm. A simple 2D die model does not capture this vertical heat path or the cooling.
The solver is 3D-ICE v3.0.0 with non-uniform initial temperature (idle or cold warmup). The cooling and package model differ from any Studio solver.

Power comes from Sniper+McPAT time-varying per-unit traces (1M-cycle steps, many units per core, plus AVX512, System Agent, IMC and I/O additions). The paper publishes no per-block power values or trace, and a one-row power trace would not reproduce workload-dependent hotspots.
The hotspot metrics (MLTD within a 1 mm radius, severity sigmoid) are not temperature-only observables. The runner's temperatures cannot be compared numerically to the paper's TUH.
There is no optimizer or controller in the original setup, and no reliability model beyond the threshold-based severity metric. These do not map onto optimizer-based or controller-based Studio flows.

Interposer, 3D stacking and chiplets are not modeled. The setup is a single monolithic 2D die (about 5 mm2 core area at 14nm), with 7 cores, node-scaled area (5/2.5/1.25 mm2 per core) and a 3x2 core aspect ratio.
No Studio package or material assumptions are provided in the packet, so none are asserted.

Any Studio placement built from dimensions and powers would be a separate illustrative 2D construction. Its generated coordinates are not paper-derived facts and must not be compared numerically with the paper's TUH.
No exact replication of the paper's results is claimed.
